QF.id: AIFM CII Fund Monitoring Reporting and Exit_8

question.text: Which exit route does Chapter 12 describe as 'by and large considered the most preferred and attractive' exit option for an equity-oriented Category I/II AIF, having historically yielded the best returns?

answer.text: Offer for Sale through an Initial Public Offer (IPO).

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 12 expressly states: 'Offer for Sale through an Initial Public Offer (IPO) is by and large considered the most preferred and attractive exit option for an equity-oriented AIF and has historically yielded the best returns.' Partial exit at IPO plus secondary-market selldown is also possible. The Trap: Strategic M&A is explicitly called the SECOND most preferred. Buyback is a last-resort / going-concern option. Corporate liquidation is the least preferred (salvage value only). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same hierarchy. For XXI-B (PMS, listed securities), IPO vs secondary-market exit is less relevant since positions are already liquid. Manager's Pro-Tip: Start IPO prep 18-24 months before target exit. Engage merchant bankers early, fix auditor rotation and corporate governance gaps (listing requirements), and time the lock-in/lock-up roll-off with your fund's winding-down phase.
